nodes.name: mlp.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the power-balance mlp model type, tuning NN width/depth, the exponential AdamW schedule (lr0, lrf, weight_decay, horizon-invariant transition_frac, decay_rate), and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean metric with hyperband early termination.
nodes.languageNotes: Sweeping huber_delta is safe here because the sweep metric val/loss.mean is the delta-free validation loss, so the sweep cannot game the metric by shrinking delta.

nodes.name: p_oh.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the ohmic-power (p_oh) submodule predictor, tuning NN width/depth and optimizer schedule parameters against val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.
nodes.languageNotes: huber_delta is deliberately NOT swept: the submodules lack a delta-free validation suite, so sweeping delta would let the sweep shrink the reported loss instead of improving predictions.

nodes.name: p_rad.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the radiated-power (p_rad) submodule predictor, tuning NN width/depth and optimizer schedule parameters against val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors p_oh.yaml; huber_delta is deliberately excluded because the submodule sweep metric is not delta-free.

nodes.name: sciml-taue-nn.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the sciml-taue-nn power-balance model (bounded NN tau_e inside the physics dW/dt balance), tuning NN width/depth, optimizer schedule, and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean metric.

nodes.name: sciml-taue-scalinglaw.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the sciml-taue-scalinglaw power-balance model; sweeps only training dynamics (optimizer schedule and huber_delta) because the scaling law has no NN hyperparameters and its p_oh/p_rad submodules are restored from their own tuned cases.
nodes.languageNotes: No model_init_config block: the H89/H98 tau_e blend is parameter-free at init, so only optimizer and loss knobs are swept.

nodes.name: transformer.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the recurrent transformer power-balance model, tuning architecture (d_model, num_heads, history_len, nn_width, nn_depth), optimizer schedule, and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean metric.
nodes.languageNotes: history_len sweeps the rolling buffer of past predicted Wtot values carried in the module's discrete state.

nodes.name: mlp.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian hyperparameter sweep definition for the profile study's unstructured MLP model type, sweeping NN width/depth and softmax temperature plus the shared optimizer (lr0/lrf/weight_decay/transition_frac/decay_rate) and Huber loss deltas, minimizing the delta-free val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.
nodes.languageNotes: transition_frac expresses the LR decay time constant as a fraction of total optimizer steps, making the tuned schedule horizon-invariant across epoch budgets and batch sizes.

nodes.name: reservoir.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the profile study's reservoir-computing model type, sweeping reservoir size, spectral radius, input scaling, leak rate, and iteration steps alongside the shared optimizer schedule and Huber loss deltas, minimizing val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.

nodes.name: shape-init-kmeans.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the profile study's kmeans-initialized B-spline shape-basis model type, sweeping NN width/depth, number of shape bases (n_shapes), and softmax temperature plus the shared optimizer schedule and Huber loss deltas, minimizing val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.

nodes.name: shape-init-pca.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the profile study's PCA-initialized B-spline shape-basis model type, identical in structure to the kmeans sweep: NN width/depth, n_shapes, and softmax temperature plus the shared optimizer schedule and Huber loss deltas, minimizing val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.

nodes.name: torax-cgm.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the profile study's TORAX critical-gradient-model (cgm) type, sweeping the shared width/depth of the three coefficient MLPs (transport, sources, edge), TORAX relaxation time t_final, and solver step count, plus the shared optimizer schedule and Huber loss deltas.
nodes.languageNotes: Comment notes activation memory scales linearly with batch size because each sample runs a differentiated multi-step TORAX simulation under vmap, ruling out full-batch training.

nodes.name: torax-constant.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the profile study's TORAX constant-transport model type, sweeping the shared coefficient-MLP width/depth, TORAX relaxation time t_final, and solver step count, plus the shared optimizer schedule and Huber loss deltas, minimizing val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.

nodes.name: torax-gyrobohm.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the profile study's TORAX gyro-Bohm transport model type, sweeping the shared coefficient-MLP width/depth, TORAX relaxation time t_final, and solver step count, plus the shared optimizer schedule and Huber loss deltas, minimizing val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.

nodes.name: torax-qlknn.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the profile study's TORAX QLKNN transport model type, sweeping the shared coefficient-MLP width/depth, TORAX relaxation time t_final, and solver step count, plus the shared optimizer schedule and Huber loss deltas, minimizing val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.

nodes.name: p_oh.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the ohmic-power (p_oh) submodule prerequisite cases of the transport study, sweeping NN width/depth and the exponential-AdamW schedule (lr0, lrf, weight_decay, horizon-invariant transition_frac, decay_rate) against val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination. huber_delta is deliberately not swept because the p_oh/p_rad submodules lack a delta-free validation suite.
nodes.languageNotes: transition_frac expresses the LR decay time constant as a fraction of total optimizer steps, so tuned schedules transfer across epoch budgets and batch sizes.

nodes.name: p_rad.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep definition for the radiated-power (p_rad) submodule prerequisite cases of the transport study, identical in structure to p_oh.yaml: NN width/depth plus optimizer schedule swept against val/loss.mean with hyperband, and huber_delta intentionally excluded because the submodule sweep metric is not delta-free.

nodes.name: power_balance.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the power_balance pseudo-model-type prerequisite cases (Wtot evolution model reused inside the transport sciml architecture), sweeping NN width/depth, the exponential-AdamW schedule, and huber_delta - safe here because the sweep metric val/loss.mean is PowerBalanceTRB's delta-free validation loss.
nodes.languageNotes: huber_delta lives under loss_config and is only sweepable for model types whose validation loss is delta-free, preventing the sweep from gaming the reported loss.

nodes.name: profile.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the profile pseudo-model-type prerequisite cases (Te/ne profile predictor reused inside the transport sciml architecture), sweeping NN width/depth, shape-basis count (n_shapes), softmax_temp, the optimizer schedule, and both huber_delta and huber_delta_grad on peak-normalized profiles against the delta-free val/loss.mean.
nodes.languageNotes: Huber deltas act on peak-normalized profiles so they read as fractional errors; a separate huber_delta_grad covers the gradient loss term.

nodes.name: sciml.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the transport sciml model type, which composes pretrained power_balance and profile submodules and has no NN of its own - so only training dynamics are swept: the exponential-AdamW schedule and huber_delta against TransportPredictorTRB's delta-free val/loss.mean.
nodes.languageNotes: No model_init_config block: architecture hyperparameters come from the submodules' own tuned prerequisite cases, restored from checkpoints.

nodes.name: torax-cgm.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the torax-cgm transport model type (differentiable TORAX step with critical-gradient-model transport), sweeping the shared width/depth of the three coefficient MLPs (transport, sources, edge), the optimizer schedule, and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean.
nodes.languageNotes: No t_final / n_solver_steps sweep: the transport predictor advances exactly one solver step of the fixed 1 ms dataset timebase per call.

nodes.name: torax-constant.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the torax-constant transport model type (differentiable TORAX step with constant transport coefficients), identical in shape to the other torax-* sweeps: coefficient-MLP width/depth, optimizer schedule, and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean.

nodes.name: torax-gyrobohm.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the torax-gyrobohm transport model type (differentiable TORAX step with gyro-Bohm transport scaling), sweeping the shared coefficient-MLP width/depth, the optimizer schedule, and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean with hyperband early termination.

nodes.name: torax-qlknn.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the torax-qlknn transport model type (differentiable TORAX step with the QLKNN turbulent-transport surrogate), sweeping the shared coefficient-MLP width/depth, the optimizer schedule, and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean.

nodes.name: transformer.yaml
nodes.summary: W&B Bayesian sweep for the transport transformer model type (recurrent causal attention over a rolling predicted-profile history buffer), sweeping attention architecture (d_model, num_heads, history_len), MLP width/depth, the optimizer schedule, and huber_delta against the delta-free val/loss.mean.
nodes.languageNotes: history_len sizes the discrete-state rolling buffer of past predicted profiles carried in the module State between steps.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what this repo does: it compares ML architectures for predicting tokamak plasma behavior (profiles, power balance, and profile evolution) and studies cross-device transfer learning between C-Mod, DIII-D, TCV, and MAST. CLAUDE.md is the deep architectural map of the codebase - it documents the Study/Case pattern, the data flow, and every module directory, and is the single best orientation document here. Together they frame the four research questions the code exists to answer: which architecture adapts best, whether historic data is needed, how many target shots suffice, and how inputs should be normalized.

tour.title: Configuration Backbone
tour.description: Before any code runs, two files shape the environment. pyproject.toml declares dependencies (JAX, xarray, the POPSIM submodule), the uv-based build, and the pytest configuration that makes the fast suite the default. config.py defines StudyConfig, a frozen Pydantic settings object read from PTPS_* environment variables and exposed through a global one-shot proxy - it is the highest fan-in file in the repo (41 incoming edges), so nearly everything you see later depends on it.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic frozen models make configuration immutable after construction. Combined with a module-level proxy object, this gives Python a safe global config: any mutation attempt raises, so tests reset it explicitly rather than leaking state.

tour.title: Device Data Workflows
tour.description: All learning starts from experimental shot data. workflow.py defines DataWorkflow, the abstract base each device implements - it fixes the raw-file variable schema (RAW_DATASET_VARS), standardizes dimension names to shot/time_idx/psi_n, and drives distributed fitting via prepare_shot/assemble_shot hooks. cmod_dataset.py is the richest concrete implementation, pulling C-Mod signals through MDSPlus, while cli.py is the Fire command-line entry point for building datasets. Per-device config.toml files (like C-Mod's) hold shotlists and paths.
tour.languageLesson: Python abstract base classes here use the template-method pattern: the base's make_raw_data_files_distributed drives the whole pipeline while subclasses supply only prepare_shot/assemble_shot. A thread pool sized by a per-device prepare_workers field handles I/O-bound staging (MAST uses 8 for S3 latency; C-Mod stays serial because its MDSplus client is not thread-safe).

tour.title: Gaussian Process Profile Fitting
tour.description: Raw Thomson-scattering measurements are noisy point clouds; the models need smooth Te/ne profiles with error bars and gradients. fit_worker.py is a self-contained mkgp Gaussian-process fitter that turns per-shot scattered data into fitted profiles, and dispatcher.py fans those fits out to a SLURM cluster in batches. dataset_creation.md documents the end-to-end recipe for producing a device dataset, tying Step 3's workflows to this fitting stage.

tour.title: Organizing Data for Training
tour.description: organize_data.py is the bridge between per-device datasets and model training: get_ds selects per-study signal preparation, concatenates shots, performs the 80/20 train/val split, reindexes filtered shots back onto the uniform 1 kHz timebase, and implements whole-dataset domain normalization for visualization. stages.py labels each timeslice as rampup, flattop, or rampdown - a segmentation the analysis machinery later uses to report stage-resolved errors. Both are heavily imported (16 and 7 incoming edges).

tour.title: The Study/Case Pattern
tour.description: study.py is the architectural heart of the repo: a Study holds many Case objects, each a unique point on a case grid (model_type x training_data x normalization x domain_adaptation x num_target_shots), with chained prerequisites so transfer cases depend on their pretrained checkpoints. The base class provides everything generic - prereq building, the make_train_config template method, the run_study CLI classmethod, and result collection - while each study subclass declares only what differs via ClassVars. Critically, str(case) names checkpoint directories, result files, and SLURM jobs, so its format is pinned by tests: byte-level drift orphans existing runs.
tour.languageLesson: Two Python dataclass traps live here: a subclass must keep its own __init__ or @dataclass silently regenerates one and drops validation, and it must alias __hash__ = Study.Case.__hash__ because @dataclass with eq=True sets __hash__ = None on the subclass.

tour.title: Input Normalization as Modules
tour.description: Research question 4 - how to normalize features from devices with little domain overlap - is answered by normalization.py. InputNormalizer is itself a POPSIM module offering raw, physics (dimensionless), per-device zscore, CORAL covariance alignment, and staged physics-coral/physics-zscore variants. Normalizers are fitted on training data only at model init and stored as frozen buffers: they checkpoint with the model but are never trainable. With 16 incoming edges, every predictor family from the next three steps builds on this file.
tour.languageLesson: In JAX/Equinox, 'frozen buffers' are pytree leaves excluded from the trainable-parameter filter: trainable selectors pick module.nn leaves explicitly, so normalizer statistics travel with checkpoints without ever receiving gradients.

tour.title: Shared Training Machinery
tour.description: trb_utils.py collects the helpers every TrainRunBuilder shares: per-case dataset selection (resolve_case_datasets), NaN-safe per-shot time integrals of error, the standard exponential AdamW optimizer plus its grouped variant that runs submodules at reduced learning rates, the validation eval suite, and the segment-based time-dependent dataloader construction. scalar_power_trb.py shows the pattern's payoff: the ohmic and radiated power predictors are subclasses that set only SIGNAL and MODULE_CLS ClassVars. This layer is why three different studies can share one training pipeline.

tour.title: Profile Predictor Models
tour.description: The first model family predicts Te/ne profiles on a uniform 51-point rho grid at a single time. module.py defines the time-independent architectures - B-spline shape bases weighted by an NN (PCA or k-means initialized), an unstructured NN, and a reservoir model - while torax_module.py wraps differentiable TORAX plasma simulations whose transport, edge, and source parameters an NN predicts; it also owns the coefficient-bounding helpers the transport predictor later imports. trb.py builds the training runs, including the deliberate loss split: training uses a swept Huber delta, validation uses delta-free error softened inside the GP-fit error bars so hyperparameter sweeps cannot game the metric.

tour.title: Power Balance Models
tour.description: The second family is time-dependent: predicting stored-energy (Wtot) evolution with a simple-Euler stepper. module.py implements four architectures spanning the physics-to-data spectrum - a tau_e scaling-law model, a hybrid SciML model (physics power balance dW/dt = P_aux + P_oh - P_rad - Wtot/tau_e with a bounded NN tau_e), a plain MLP, and a recurrent transformer that carries a rolling buffer of its own past predictions as discrete state. The SciML variants hold p_oh/p_rad submodule predictors (Step 8's ScalarPowerTRB subclasses) restored from prerequisite-case checkpoints and anchored to measured signals during joint training. trb.py wires all of this into train runs.
tour.languageLesson: The transformer keeps its prediction history as a discrete_no_save_field in the module State - JAX requires all state to be explicit pytree data, so 'memory' becomes a rolling buffer threaded through each step. A learned per-slot position embedding is essential: scalar tokens are otherwise permutation-invariant to attention.

tour.title: Transport Predictor Models
tour.description: The third family is the study's capstone: full profile evolution over time. module.py composes the previous two - its sciml model type nests a trained PowerBalance module (for the Wtot state) and a trained ProfilePredictor (fed the state-implied betan), with anchor losses tying intermediate predictions to measured signals; a transformer variant carries a profile-history buffer, and torax-* variants run one real TORAX solver step per 1 ms timeslice, feeding measured P_aux directly and letting the NN predict only deposition shape, fueling, and a Beer-Lambert absorption fraction. train_configs.py builds the one-step TORAX configuration, and trb.py reuses the profile study's evaluation machinery.

tour.title: The Three Study Packages
tour.description: Now the entry points make sense. Each study module subclasses Step 6's Study with a thin Case and Config: profile_study.py is the reference implementation, power_balance_study.py mirrors it, and transport_transfer_study.py has the deepest prerequisite chain (sciml -> power_balance + profile pseudo-model-type cases -> p_oh + p_rad). Each is a Fire CLI run as python -m transport_study.<study> run_study --config=study.toml. Per-model-type W&B sweep configs like sciml.yaml define the hyperparameter searches whose tuned results merge into every case's train config.
tour.languageLesson: Fire generates the CLI directly from the run_study classmethod signature, so command-line flags live in exactly one place: adding a parameter to the base classmethod adds the flag to all three studies at once.

tour.title: Analysis and Reporting
tour.description: After training, each study produces stage-resolved metrics, per-case PDF reports, and per-axis comparison tables. case_analysis.py is the generic SLURM fan-out driver launching one CPU analysis job per finished case; the power balance study's study_metrics.py computes time-averaged stage errors (so long shots do not score worse by raw integral) and its case_reports.py renders best/worst holdout-shot PDFs - the transport study re-exports this machinery wholesale. tables.py in orchestration holds the generic grouping/markdown/csv comparison-table writer each study parameterizes with a ComparisonTableSpec.

tour.title: Cluster and Experiment Infrastructure
tour.description: Everything above runs at scale on a SLURM cluster with Weights & Biases tracking. slurm_utils.py submits and monitors training and analysis jobs (including killing stuck or long-pending ones), wandb_utils.py manages sweep creation and tuned-config retrieval, and data_visualization.py provides the shared hazard-extrapolation and domain-overlap plots that each study subclasses to visualize its own feature space before training begins - a direct look at the cross-device domain gap the whole project is about.

tour.title: Test Suite Architecture
tour.description: The tests mirror the package layout and encode the project's contracts. conftest.py resets the global config around every test and exposes the make_stub_study factory; stubs.py provides the StubStudy/StubCase that orchestration tests drive instead of building a real case grid. Cross-study behavior is tested once: test_study_config.py parametrizes the config-lock and TOML round trip over all three studies, and test_sweep_configs.py validates every sweep YAML against each Case's VALID_MODEL_TYPES. The fast suite (uv run pytest) excludes anything marked slow - training, TORAX runs, or real device data.
tour.languageLesson: pytest markers plus addopts = -m 'not slow' in pyproject.toml make the fast suite the default: expensive GPU tests exist in the same tree but only run when explicitly selected with -m slow.
